quizzes.title: Module 1 — Tuesday — Editing to Beats
quizzes.description: Tuesday's quiz covers the beat feature in CapCut, generating beat markers automatically and manually, splitting clips at beat points, beat-detection intensity, and keeping visual changes aligned with the music.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the beat feature in CapCut Mobile?
options: To increase the resolution of a video
To remove background noise from music
To synchronize video cuts and editing changes with the rhythm of music
To automatically add subtitles to a video
questions.explanation: The beat feature exists to align your edits with the music. It finds the rhythm so your cuts and visual changes land where the track does.

questions.prompt: After selecting a music track in CapCut, where can you find the option to generate beat markers, as demonstrated in the lesson?
options: In the music track's editing options
In the export settings
In the text editing menu
In the device's general settings
questions.explanation: Beat detection belongs to the audio, so the option lives in the music track's own editing options rather than anywhere in the video or export settings.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between automatically generating beats and generating them manually?
options: Automatic generation adds transitions, while manual generation adds text.
Automatic generation detects beat points for you, while manual generation lets you identify and mark them yourself.
Automatic generation works only with videos, while manual generation works only with images.
Automatic generation changes the aspect ratio, while manual generation changes the resolution.
questions.explanation: Automatic detection does the finding for you. Manual generation leaves the marking to your own ear, which is useful when the track is unusual or you want a specific feel.

questions.prompt: In the lesson, what happens when the editor splits a video clip at a beat marker?
options: The entire video is automatically exported.
The music track is permanently deleted.
The video changes from landscape to portrait.
The clip is divided at that point, allowing the editor to make changes or arrange footage around the beat.
questions.explanation: Splitting at a beat marker cuts the clip at that exact moment, which gives you a new edge to work from — you can rearrange footage, trim it, or apply changes there.

questions.prompt: Why might an editor choose a more intense beat-detection setting?
options: To identify more beat points in the music
To remove every silent moment from the video
To make the music louder automatically
To prevent the editor from splitting clips
questions.explanation: A more intense setting picks up more beat points, giving you a denser set of markers. That suits fast, busy edits where you want cuts to land more often.

questions.prompt: An editor is creating a dance video and wants visual changes to happen in time with the music. How can beat markers help?
options: They automatically guarantee that every effect will look professional.
They remove the need to arrange clips.
They provide reference points for timing cuts and visual changes to the music.
They automatically replace the original footage with new clips.
questions.explanation: Beat markers are reference points, not decisions. They show you where the music lands so you can place cuts and visual changes on those moments.

questions.prompt: According to the lesson, what can an editor do after splitting footage at selected beat points?
options: Only change the video's file name
Add or arrange other clips, trim footage, or apply changes such as transformations and effects
Change the music into a video file
Export the project without choosing any settings
questions.explanation: The split is the beginning, not the end. Once a clip is divided at a beat you can arrange, trim, transform or add effects to the sections you have created.

questions.prompt: While editing to a song, you notice that a visual change happens slightly before the beat you intended to match. What is the best approach?
options: Increase the video's resolution until the timing improves.
Add more music tracks to hide the timing problem.
Leave it unchanged because visual changes should never match musical beats.
Adjust the cut or visual change so it aligns more closely with the intended beat marker.
questions.explanation: Timing problems are solved by adjusting timing. Nudge the cut or the visual change onto the beat marker — resolution and extra tracks have nothing to do with it.
